newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Paranagua port strike to enter 2nd day.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Paranagua port strike to enter 2nd day.

text.p: Dockworkers at Paranagua, a key Brazilian port for grain shipments, will remain on strike for another day at least, after negotiators failed to reach an agreement over a pay dispute Wednesday evening, a port authority official said.
"The strike is continuing. For the time being, it will last 72 hours. Negotiations will carry on tomorrow, however, and who knows, there may be a resolution," the official said.
The work stoppage began at 1200 local/1500 GMT Wednesday, paralysing the port's mechanized grain terminal and other operations.
Dockworkers are seeking a 21 percent pay increase, which they say they have been owed since last year.

Earlier this week there was talk that workers at other ports in the country would stage sympathy strikes. But an official from the National Dockworkers Union said Wednesday there would be no national stoppage.
((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
